cues: Here is context almost no guide gives you.

The poem was commissioned in nineteen ninety nine by Oxfam for a millennium project called On The Line, which linked schools and communities along the Greenwich Meridian, the line of zero longitude, from Britain down through France, Spain, and West Africa.
That explains the first line: O ye who travel the meridian line.
So it is not a war poem, and not really about labour migration: its subject is rich and poor countries at the end of the century.
